truthAudit.Summary: Audit of the Run 1 answer against 20 ground-truth vulnerabilities. 10 true vulnerabilities were detected by the previous answer (all as found_full, but several with wrong severity/CWE/impact that are recorded as corrections). 10 true vulnerabilities were missed (CWE-798, CWE-338, CWE-362 static-tm race, CWE-377, CWE-613, CWE-754, CWE-674, CWE-362 result-cache race, CWE-367 TOCTOU, CWE-369). 3 of the previous answer's 14 findings are overclaims or unsupported: the exec command-injection finding (CWE-78), the null-pointer-dereference finding (CWE-476), and the safe_string_copy off-by-one finding (CWE-120), none of which is among the 20 true vulnerabilities. Net result: 50% detection coverage with 3 unsupported findings.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Format String Vulnerability in Audit Log Function — CWE-132, High — "Lines 237-238: std::string active_format = runtime_log_format();  printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input);"
Items.Notes: Found the runtime log format string reached by printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input) at source lines 0237-0238, configurable via log_format in supercalc.conf. Correctly identified the mechanism.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer Overflow in Recursive Factorial — CWE-192, Low — "result is a plain long long with no overflow check, so multiplying past LLONG_MAX is signed-integer overflow (undefined behavior)."
Items.Notes: Found the unbounded factorial loop (result *= i at source line 0317) and its UB. Correct defect, but severity Low is understated (truth: High) and CWE-192 is wrong (truth: CWE-190).

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-After-Free Between Pool Cleanup and Deferred History Tasks — CWE-476, High — "cleanup() frees every owns_memory block (line 174-176) before the queued workers wake and dereference scratch."
Items.Notes: Found the UAF: stage_deferred_history_flush() enqueues tasks sleeping 25ms over pool-allocated scratch buffers (source lines 0817-0824), then cleanup() frees all owned blocks (source lines 0172-0182). Correct defect; severity should be Critical and CWE-416, not CWE-476.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Command Injection in Config Validator — CWE-78, High — "std::string command = validator_cmd + " " + config_file;   int result = system(command.c_str());"
Items.Notes: Found command injection through validate_config() at source lines 0563-0569, with attacker-controlled config values concatenated into system(). Correct defect; severity should be Critical, not High.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Heap Buffer Overflow from Inverted Bounds Check in evaluate_expression — CWE-120, High — "The unsafe strcpy branch is taken for every expression of length >= 1024 (sizeof(input_buffer_), line 664). safe_string_copy in the else branch correctly caps to dest_size, but the if branch has the comparison inverted and needs length <= 1023."
Items.Notes: Found the inverted bounds check routing expressions of length >= 1024 to strcpy(input_buffer_, expression.c_str()) at source lines 0831-0835, where input_buffer_ is the 1024-byte member char array (source line 0664). Live defect, correctly evidenced. Note: the answer split this one true vulnerability into a second finding (safe_string_copy off-by-one), which is an overclaim of detection credit; the second was also judged unsupported in this build. Location correction: input_buffer_ is a stack member of the stack-allocated SuperCalc object in main(), so this is a stack overflow.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data Race in ThreadSafeCounter::increment — CWE-367, Low — "The volatile read at line 483 occurs outside the lock, so concurrent callers can load the same base value; the mutex only serializes the write at line 486, losing increments. volatile is not an atomic fence and provides no synchronization."
Items.Notes: Found the lost-update race (volatile long long value_ at source line 0478; old_value = value_ outside the lock, value_ = old_value + 1 inside). Correct defect; truth rates it CWE-362 and Medium, not CWE-367/Low. The previous answer also softened the impact claim ("No direct confidentiality/integrity impact"), which is recorded as an impact correction.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Authentication Bypass via EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE Backdoor — CWE-287 / CWE-614, High — "if (login_attempts_ > 5) {   if (input.find("EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE") != std::string::npos) {     authenticated_ = true;"
Items.Notes: Found the authentication bypass at source lines 0592-0599 where EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE sets authenticated_=true after 5 failures. This is the same defect truth classifies as a CWE-511 logic bomb; the answer should have been titled as such, and the CWE should be CWE-511 instead of CWE-287/CWE-614.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Path Traversal in Config File Loader — CWE-22, High — "std::string full_path = config_dir_ + filename;   if (!std::filesystem::exists(full_path)) return false;   std::ifstream file(full_path);"
Items.Notes: Found path traversal through load_config() at source lines 0542-0547 (config_dir_ + filename opened without traversal rejection). Correct defect; truth rates it CWE-22/Medium, not High (the High severity was derived from conflation with the validator injection, not from the traversal itself).

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Heap Buffer Overflow in ExpressionParser::parse strcpy into Fixed Pool Buffer — CWE-120, High — "buffer_size_ = 256;   expression_buffer_ = static_cast<char*>(memory::g_memory_pool.allocate(buffer_size_)); ...  for (const auto& token : tokens) expr_str += token.text + " ";   if (expr_str.length() > 0) strcpy(expression_buffer_, expr_str.c_str());"
Items.Notes: Found the unbounded strcpy into a 256-byte heap block at source lines 0366-0376, with evidence (token text is never size-checked). Correct defect; severity should be Critical and CWE-122, not CWE-120/High.

The hardcoded administrator credential ADMIN_SECRET (source line 0073: constexpr char ADMIN_SECRET[] = "SC_ENT_2025_AUTH") is never reported as a vulnerability, even though the same literal appears in the previous answer's trigger text ("via secret 'SC_ENT_2025_AUTH' ...", source line 0590). No session-token-exposure finding exists. CWE-798 missed.

generate_session_token() (source lines 0635-0640) uses std::mt19937 seeded from std::random_device and uniform_int_distribution(1000, 9999) — only 10^4 possible tokens, ~13 bits of entropy. Not reported anywhere; CWE-338 missed.

log_debug_message() holds a static std::tm cached_time (source line 0230) and is callable from thread-pool workers alongside the main thread, so localtime() results are read/written without synchronization. The previous answer reported a thread-safety race only for ThreadSafeCounter, not this timestamp cache; CWE-362 missed.

append_override_audit_event() (source lines 0622-0633) builds "sh -c \"echo Admin override logged >> " + TMPDIR/TMPDIR-controlled audit_path and calls system(command.c_str()) — both command injection and write to an uncontrolled temporary path. The previous answer never analyzed this helper; CWE-377/CWE-78 missed.

session_token_ (source line 0580) and the process-global static login_attempts_ (source line 0582) persist across sessions; no finding covers token reuse, rollback or reset of failed-attempt state (the answer only mentions the shared counter once, in a remediation suggestion, never as a defect). CWE-613 missed.

handle_variable_command() (source lines 0725-0738) parses tokens and calls std::stod(tokens[3]) with no validation, no bounds check and no exception handler (evaluate_expression has a try/catch at 0875-0878, the variable handler does not). CWE-754 missed.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unsigned Integer Underflow in Memory Pool Fragment Size — CWE-192 / CWE-122, Medium — "size_t remaining = previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES; ... if (remaining > 32) {"
Items.Notes: Found the unsigned underflow in MemoryPool::allocate() at source lines 0132-0142: remaining = previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES wraps when size is within 64 bytes of the block, and the > 32 test only guards against 0. Correct defect; truth rates it CWE-191 and Critical, not CWE-192/CWE-122 and Medium.

parse_expression() and parse_factor() recurse through parentheses with no depth guard; config::limits::MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH = 256 (source line 0065) is defined but never read by the parser (source lines 0381-0433). CWE-674 missed.

ExpressionEvaluator::evaluate_cached() reads/writes result_cache_ (source line 0440) and calls evaluate_cached() from thread-pool tasks (source line 0808) while caching runs unsynchronized — cache_mutex_ is never taken in evaluate_cached(). CWE-362 result-cache race missed.

load_config() exists() at source line 0544, sleeps 25ms (source line 0545), then opens the same path (source line 0546). The answer reported the path traversal that includes these lines, but never characterized the sleep/open race as a TOCTOU or a DoS vector; CWE-367 missed.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Division by Zero in calculate_route_score — CWE-547, High — "return 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length);  For an empty input, find_first_of returns npos and token_length = input.length() = 0, so the division by 100/0 (line 752) raises SIGFPE."
Items.Notes: Found the zero-divisor at source lines 0749-0753 with correct trigger reasoning (empty input, no whitespace, token_length==0). Correct defect; truth rates it CWE-369 and Low, not CWE-547 and High. The claim that the unsigned division "traps on x86" is also an incorrect impact claim.
